item.text:
**Verdict:** Strongly negative. Putin’s 2023 rule reduced insecurity for loyalists in narrow ways, but the broader pattern was fear management through repression, war, and public intimidation rather than a genuine reduction in domestic fear without state terror.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia | The report says antiwar protesters and opposition figures were jailed, NGOs were forced to close, media were restricted, and 844 criminal cases were opened for antiwar expression. That is evidence of a broad political fear climate, not reduced domestic insecurity. | 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.1 |
| Russia crosses new lines in crackdown on Putin's enemies | Reuters via Investing.com | 21 Apr 2023 | https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/analysisrussia-crosses-new-lines-in-crackdown-on-putins-enemies-2992615 | Reuters described security services and courts as crossing new thresholds in a campaign against perceived enemies, spies, and traitors. This shows domestic fear being produced through repression rather than replaced with ordinary security. | 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.1 |
| Russian parliament votes to introduce life sentences for treason | Reuters via Investing.com | 18 Apr 2023 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russian-parliament-votes-to-introduce-life-sentences-for-treason-3058140 | Russia raised treason to a life sentence and increased penalties for sabotage and terrorism. That is classic escalation of coercive legal controls, not a narrow safety measure that lowers fear. | 3B.6, 3B.5 |
| Putin signs Russian law establishing electronic draft call-up | Reuters via Yahoo News | 14 Apr 2023 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/putin-signs-russian-law-establishing-195445933.html | The electronic draft system made conscription more efficient and harder to evade. It is a control tool tied to mobilization pressure, not a confidence-building domestic security reform. | 3B.6, 3B.5, 2B.8 |
| Putin says he let mutiny continue to avoid bloodshed | Reuters via Investing.com | 26 Jun 2023 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russias-putin-says-he-let-mutiny-continue-to-avoid-bloodshed-3113594 | Putin said he deliberately allowed the Wagner mutiny to run its course to avoid bloodshed. This is the main restraint-adjacent evidence, but it is a narrow crisis-management choice and does not amount to a broader reduction in political fear. | 3B.6, 2B.5 |
| 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia | The same report says authorities used new laws to punish dissent and independent expression, jailed opposition figures, and used the “discrediting the military” laws widely and indiscriminately. That is direct evidence of replacing insecurity with state intimidation. | 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.1 |
| Putin said Russia was ready for talks and African proposals deserved attention | Kremlin | 28 Jul 2023 | https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/71826 | Putin used conditional peace-talk language, but it did not soften the internal fear climate or show a move away from intimidation at home. It is only weak counterevidence. | 3B.6, 2B.7 |
| Putin and Xi issued a joint statement welcoming dialogue on Ukraine | Kremlin | 21 Mar 2023 | https://special.kremlin.ru/supplement/5920 | The statement endorsed dialogue and warned against uncontrolled escalation. This is diplomatic language, but it does not show domestic fear reduction or a break from coercive governance. | 3B.6, 2B.7 |

**Search gap:** I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin systematically reduced domestic fear and insecurity in a way that avoided substituting state terror, repression, or a wider climate of political intimidation. The best counterevidence is limited to narrow crisis containment and conditional diplomacy, not a broader domestic de-escalation.
